question.text: Kiran's retirement corpus of Rs.80,00,000 is invested entirely in bank FDs at 7%. Inflation is 6%. The purchasing power of her annual nominal interest income, expressed in today's terms, is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (pp.20, 74), the workbook computes real return by adjusting nominal return for inflation. Nominal annual interest = Rs.80,00,000 x 7% = Rs.5,60,000. Adjusted to today's purchasing power: Rs.5,60,000 / 1.06 = approximately Rs.5,28,302, i.e. ~Rs.5,28,000. The Trap: Rs.5,60,000 is the nominal income and overstates real purchasing power; Rs.1,50,943 does not correspond to the workbook's real-return computation against this stem. Note: Always present returns to retirees in both nominal and real terms — the gap shows why some inflation-beating allocation is usually necessary.
